name: Ankle Circles with Single Leg Balance
pose_description: Stand on one leg with a slight knee bend, arms out to sides for balance. Keep your standing leg stable and engaged.
end_pose_description: The standing leg maintains its slight knee bend and engagement, with arms remaining out to the sides for balance. The non-standing foot is pointed downwards, with the sole turned outwards, visibly engaging the calf and outer shin muscles as the ankle reaches peak plantarflexion and eversion.

name: Bird Dog
pose_description: Balancing on the left hand and right knee. The RIGHT arm reaches straight out in front, parallel to the ground, and the LEFT leg extends straight behind, also parallel to the ground. The body forms a straight line from fingertips to toes.
end_pose_description: On all fours in a tabletop position on the ground. The right arm is extended fully forward, parallel to the ground. The left leg is extended fully backward, parallel to the ground. The back is flat and level. Only the left hand and right knee remain on the ground.

name: Bird Dog Hold with Scapular Punch
pose_description: On hands and knees with right arm extended forward and left leg extended behind, parallel to the floor, in a standard bird dog position. From this hold, the extended arm performs a scapular punch by protracting the shoulder blade forward, pushing the hand further away from the body, then retracting back. The spine remains neutral and the core is fully braced.
end_pose_description: The athlete is in a quadruped position with the right arm fully extended forward and slightly protracted, with the shoulder blade pushed forward away from the torso, while the left leg remains extended straight behind parallel to the floor. The core, glutes, and shoulder stabilizers are visibly engaged with a rigid, neutral spine, and the person faces downward toward the ground with their gaze neutral.

name: Bird Dog with Stability Hold
pose_description: Start on your hands and knees with wrists under shoulders and knees under hips. Keep your head in a neutral position looking down at the floor.
end_pose_description: Extend one arm forward and the opposite leg backward until both are parallel to the floor. Maintain a level spine and neutral head position, holding for 2-3 seconds.

name: Bird Dog with Core Stability Focus
pose_description: On hands and knees in tabletop position with wrists directly under shoulders and knees under hips. The right arm extends forward and the left leg extends behind, both parallel to the floor, with an emphasis on maintaining a perfectly level pelvis and neutral spine. The movement is slow and deliberate with a prolonged hold at full extension, core braced throughout.
end_pose_description: The body forms a straight line from the extended right fingertips through the torso to the extended left heel, both limbs parallel to the floor at shoulder and hip height respectively, while the supporting left arm and right knee remain vertically aligned beneath the shoulders and hips. The core muscles are visibly tensioned, the pelvis is perfectly level with no rotation, and the spine maintains neutral alignment with the head in line with the extended arm. The person's torso is parallel to the ground with no sagging or hiking of the hips.

name: Bulgarian Split Squat
pose_description: Standing about two feet in front of a bench or elevated surface with the top of one foot resting on the bench behind. The front foot is flat on the floor. The body lowers by bending the front knee to approximately 90 degrees while the back knee drops toward the floor. The torso stays upright, and the front knee tracks over the toes.
end_pose_description: The front leg is bent to approximately 90 degrees at the knee with the thigh nearly parallel to the ground, while the back knee hovers just above the floor in a deep lunge position. The torso remains upright and vertical, perpendicular to the ground, with the front quad and glute visibly tensed and engaged. The person faces forward with weight distributed through the front foot, creating a stable asymmetrical stance.

name: Dead Bug
pose_description: Lying flat on back with arms extended straight toward the ceiling above the shoulders and both hips and knees bent to 90 degrees in a tabletop position. One arm reaches overhead toward the floor behind while the opposite leg extends straight out, lowering toward the floor without touching. The lower back remains pressed firmly into the ground throughout.
end_pose_description: The person lies supine on their back with one arm extended straight overhead toward the floor behind the head (shoulder flexed approximately 180 degrees) while the opposite leg extends fully straight, hovering just above the ground with the hip flexed at near 0 degrees; simultaneously, the other arm remains bent at 90 degrees with the hand reaching toward the ceiling and the opposite leg stays in the tabletop position with hip and knee both at 90 degrees. The lower back remains pressed flat against the ground, creating a diagonal line of tension across the torso from the extended arm to the extended leg, with visible abdominal and core musculature engaged to maintain spinal stability.

name: Dead Bug with Dumbbell
pose_description: Lie on your back with your arms extended straight up toward the ceiling holding a light dumbbell with both hands, and your hips and knees bent at 90 degrees. Your lower back is neutral against the floor.
end_pose_description: Lie on your back with both arms fully extended overhead, holding the dumbbell just above the floor, and one leg extended straight out with the heel hovering just above the floor. The other hip and knee remain bent at 90 degrees. Your lower back is pressed firmly into the floor, showcasing visible engagement of your abdominal muscles and a stretch in your latissimus dorsi.

name: Dead Bug with Shoulder Reach
pose_description: Lie flat on your back with hips and knees bent to 90 degrees, bringing your shins parallel to the floor. Extend both arms straight up towards the ceiling, hands positioned directly over your shoulders. Ensure your lower back remains pressed into the floor.
end_pose_description: The person lies supine with their lower back pressed flat against the floor, one arm extended overhead (nearly parallel to the ground) while the opposite leg extends straight out at hip height, creating a long diagonal line through the body. The reaching arm shows pronounced shoulder protraction with the scapula visibly lifted off the ribcage, while the core, obliques, and stabilizer muscles are clearly engaged to maintain the extended position and spinal stability.

name: Dumbbell Bulgarian Split Squat
pose_description: Stand facing away from a bench or elevated surface with one foot elevated behind you on the bench, holding dumbbells at your sides. Your front leg is straight with feet positioned to allow for a deep lunge.
end_pose_description: The body is lowered until the front thigh is roughly parallel to the ground, with the front knee deeply bent and the shin vertical. The rear knee is also bent, hovering just above the ground, with the hip flexors of the rear leg visibly stretched. The glutes and quadriceps of the front leg are strongly engaged, maintaining an upright torso with dumbbells held at the sides.

name: Dumbbell Lateral Raise to Single Leg Stand
pose_description: Stand on one leg with a slight knee bend, holding dumbbells at your sides with arms straight. Your non-standing leg is lightly touching the ground for light balance support if needed.
end_pose_description: Both arms are raised straight out to your sides, parallel to the floor, holding the dumbbells. Your non-standing leg is lifted off the ground with the knee bent and thigh parallel to the floor; the deltoids and gluteal muscles of your standing leg are visibly engaged.

name: Dumbbell Single-Arm Row
pose_description: Stand with feet hip-width apart, holding a dumbbell in your right hand with arm extended down. Hinge slightly at the hips with a neutral spine and brace your core.
end_pose_description: Pull the dumbbell up toward your hip, driving your elbow back and squeezing your back muscles. Lower the dumbbell with control back to the starting position.

name: Dumbbell Single-Leg Deadlift
pose_description: Stand upright on one leg with a slight bend in the standing knee. Hold a dumbbell in the hand opposite your standing leg, keeping your arm extended downwards. Maintain a straight back and lifted chest.
end_pose_description: Hinge at the hip while extending your free leg behind you for counterbalance, lowering the dumbbell toward the ground. Return to standing by driving through your heel and squeezing your glute.

name: Dumbbell Single Leg Deadlifts
pose_description: Stand on the affected leg holding a dumbbell in the opposite hand with arm at your side. The other leg is positioned for balance with a slight bend in the standing knee.
end_pose_description: Hinge at the hip while extending the non-standing leg behind you for counterbalance, lowering the dumbbell toward the ground. The torso leans forward while maintaining a neutral spine and stable ankle.

name: Glute Bridge Single Leg
pose_description: Lie on your back with knees bent and feet flat, hip-width apart. Lift one foot slightly off the ground and extend that leg slightly forward.
end_pose_description: Drive through the heel of your planted foot to lift your hips high off the ground, maintaining a straight line from knee to shoulder. Squeeze your glutes at the top before lowering back down.

name: Half-Kneeling Single-Arm Dumbbell Press
pose_description: Kneel on one knee with the opposite foot forward in a staggered stance, keeping your torso upright. Hold a dumbbell at shoulder height on one side with your elbow at 90 degrees.
end_pose_description: Press the dumbbell straight up overhead while maintaining a neutral spine and preventing any rotation of your torso. Lower the dumbbell back to shoulder height under control.

name: Half Kneeling Single-Arm Dumbbell Row
pose_description: Position yourself in a half-kneeling stance with one knee down and one foot forward, holding a dumbbell in the hand opposite your forward leg. Your torso is upright and core is engaged.
end_pose_description: Row the dumbbell up toward your hip by driving your elbow back and retracting your scapula, keeping your torso stable and square. Your shoulder blade pulls toward your spine at the top of the movement.

name: Half-Kneeling Single-Arm Row with Band
pose_description: Kneel on your right knee with left foot forward, holding a resistance band anchored at chest height in front of you. Your arm is extended straight out with the band at medium tension.
end_pose_description: Pull the band toward your ribcage by driving your elbow back, squeezing your shoulder blade toward your spine. Your torso remains upright and stable with minimal rotation.

name: Mouth Corner Lift - Alternating
pose_description: Sit facing a mirror with a neutral facial expression and relaxed lips. Keep your head still and your shoulders down.
end_pose_description: Slowly lift one corner of your mouth upward, hold for 2 seconds, then release and repeat on the opposite side. Perform 10-15 alternating repetitions while monitoring symmetry.

name: Quadruped Alternating Arm Raise
pose_description: Start on your hands and knees with hands under shoulders and knees under hips, maintaining a neutral spine. Keep your core engaged and look down to maintain neck alignment.
end_pose_description: Slowly raise one arm forward to shoulder height while keeping your body stable and level. Return to starting position and alternate sides in a controlled manner.

name: Quadruped with Alternating Leg Lifts
pose_description: Start on your hands and knees with wrists under shoulders and knees under hips. Maintain a neutral spine and engage your pelvic floor.
end_pose_description: Extend one leg behind you while keeping the pelvic floor engaged and core tight. Return to start and alternate legs, avoiding any arching in the lower back.

name: Quadruped Alternating Limb Raises
pose_description: Start on your hands and knees with wrists under shoulders and knees under hips. Keep your spine neutral and core engaged.
end_pose_description: Extend your right arm forward and left leg backward to form a straight line with your body. Hold for 2 seconds, return to start, and repeat on the opposite side.

name: Quadruped Bird-Dog with Band
pose_description: Start on hands and knees with wrists under shoulders and knees under hips. A resistance band is wrapped around one foot and held in your opposite hand.
end_pose_description: Extend your opposite arm forward and leg backward in line with your body while the band provides resistance. Maintain a level hips and neutral spine throughout the movement.

name: Single-Arm Dumbbell Overhead Press
pose_description: Stand with feet shoulder-width apart holding a dumbbell at shoulder height with your elbow slightly in front of your body. Your core is braced and your scapulae are packed.
end_pose_description: Press the dumbbell overhead in a slight forward angle, allowing your scapula to upwardly rotate naturally at the end. Your arm is fully extended with controlled stability throughout the entire range of motion.

name: Single Leg Balance
pose_description: Standing upright on one leg with the standing knee slightly soft, not locked. The opposite foot is lifted a few inches off the ground with the knee bent. Arms can be at sides or extended for balance, torso is upright, and the gaze is directed forward at a fixed point.
end_pose_description: The person stands vertically balanced on one leg with a slightly bent knee, while the opposite leg is lifted with the knee bent at approximately 90 degrees and the thigh parallel to the ground. The torso remains upright and centered over the standing leg, with visible core engagement, while the arms are either extended outward at shoulder height or positioned for counterbalance, and the head faces forward with eyes fixed on a point ahead.

name: Single-Leg Balance with Band Support
pose_description: Stand upright holding a resistance band at chest height with both hands, securing it to a sturdy object or wall mount at shoulder level. Your feet are hip-width apart.
end_pose_description: The body is balanced on one foot, with the opposite knee bent to approximately 90 degrees and the foot lifted directly off the floor, positioned just in front of the standing leg's knee. The resistance band is held firmly at chest height with both hands, maintaining a neutral spine and level hips. The gluteus medius and minimus of the standing leg are actively engaged, alongside the intrinsic foot muscles and deep core stabilizers.

name: Single-Leg Balance with Dumbbell
pose_description: Stand on one leg while holding a dumbbell at your side, with a slight knee bend in the standing leg. Keep your core tight and focus on a fixed point ahead.
end_pose_description: Maintain single-leg balance while performing small controlled arm movements with the dumbbell. Keep the supporting knee soft and engaged throughout the hold.

name: Single Leg Balance with Dumbbell Hold
pose_description: Stand on one leg with a slight knee bend, holding a dumbbell in the hand opposite your standing leg. Your non-standing knee is lifted to hip height, creating an athletic stance.
end_pose_description: Your standing leg maintains a slight knee bend, with the quadriceps and glutes visibly engaged for stability. The torso leans forward, nearly parallel to the floor, while the non-standing leg extends straight backward, also parallel to the floor. The dumbbell arm hangs naturally toward the floor, and the core muscles are contracted to hold this balanced posture.

name: Single Leg Balance on Firm Surface
pose_description: Stand upright with feet together, arms at your sides or extended for light balance. Look straight ahead at a fixed point.
end_pose_description: Lift one leg off the ground, bending the knee to 90 degrees while maintaining an upright torso. Keep the standing leg straight and engaged.

name: Single-Leg Balance on Foam Pad
pose_description: Stand upright on a foam balance pad or unstable surface with feet hip-width apart, arms at your sides. Distribute your weight evenly on both feet.
end_pose_description: The body is balanced upright on one foot on the foam pad, with the opposite knee bent and the foot hovering just above the pad. The standing leg's knee is slightly flexed, and the arms remain at the sides. The ankle stabilizers of the standing foot, core muscles, and hip abductors are visibly engaged to maintain equilibrium.

name: Single-Leg Balance Hold
pose_description: Stand upright with feet hip-width apart and arms at your sides or extended for balance. Weight is evenly distributed between both feet.
end_pose_description: The body stands upright, balanced entirely on one foot with weight distributed solely onto the supporting leg. The non-supporting foot is lifted just off the floor, with the knee slightly bent, while arms remain at the sides or extended for stability. The gluteus medius, quadriceps, hamstrings, and intrinsic foot muscles of the standing leg are visibly engaged, alongside core stabilizers maintaining an erect posture.

name: Single Leg Balance with Perturbations
pose_description: Stand on the affected leg with knee slightly bent and arms out to the sides for balance. The opposite leg is lifted with hip and knee bent to about 90 degrees.
end_pose_description: Maintain single leg stance while gently swaying side to side and forward/backward with controlled movements. Weight is centered over the affected ankle with engaged core.

name: Single-Leg Balance on Soft Surface
pose_description: Stand on one leg on a soft, unstable surface such as a cushion, folded towel, or foam pad. Keep your arms out to the sides for balance and focus your eyes on a fixed point ahead.
end_pose_description: The body holds a still, upright position on the standing leg atop the soft surface, with arms extended laterally and eyes fixed on a point ahead. The ankle stabilizers, notably the peroneals and tibialis muscles, are visibly tense, alongside engaged gluteus medius of the standing leg and core muscles, all working to maintain the full body's balance.

name: Single-Leg Balance on Stable Surface
pose_description: Stand on one leg with your knee slightly bent, arms at your sides or extended for balance. Keep your gaze focused on a fixed point ahead.
end_pose_description: The body rests stably on one leg, its knee slightly bent and ankle firm, with the non-weight-bearing foot suspended clear of the ground and its knee bent to roughly 90 degrees. Gaze is focused on a fixed point ahead, arms are at the sides or extended for balance, and the standing leg's calf muscles (gastrocnemius, soleus) and gluteus medius are visibly taut.

name: Single-Leg Balance on Unstable Surface
pose_description: Stand on one leg with your hands on your hips or extended for light balance assistance. Keep your core tight and your standing leg slightly bent at the knee.
end_pose_description: The body maintains a stable, upright posture on the unstable surface, with hands remaining on the hips or extended for assistance. The core is engaged to prevent torso sway, and the standing leg remains slightly bent at the knee. The ankle and calf muscles of the standing leg are visibly taut, actively stabilizing the body, while the opposite foot is suspended off the ground, with its knee bent at approximately 90 degrees.

name: Single-Leg Balance with Hip Activation
pose_description: Standing on one leg with the standing knee slightly soft and the hip of the standing leg actively engaged. The non-standing leg lifts with the knee bent and the hip moves through small ranges of flexion, extension, or abduction to challenge balance. Arms may be at sides or on hips, the torso is upright, and the gaze is fixed on a point ahead.
end_pose_description: The camera captures a figure standing tall on one straight leg with the standing hip and glute visibly engaged and stable, while the non-standing leg is lifted with the knee bent at approximately 90 degrees and the hip abducted, extended, or flexed to its endpoint depending on the movement pattern. The torso remains upright and vertical with no lateral lean, the core appears engaged and tight, and the gaze is directed straight ahead at a fixed point.

name: Supine Single Leg Bridges
pose_description: Lie on your back with one knee bent and foot flat on the floor, the other leg extended toward the ceiling. Arms at your sides for support.
end_pose_description: Drive through the bent leg to lift your hips off the ground into a bridge position. Hold for 2 seconds at the top.

name: Single Leg Calf Raise
pose_description: Standing on one leg with the other foot lifted off the ground, holding a wall or railing for balance. The heel of the standing foot rises as high as possible, pushing up onto the ball of the foot. The knee remains straight, the body stays tall, and the calf muscle fully contracts at the top.
end_pose_description: The person stands tall and upright on the ball of one foot with the heel lifted as high as possible, creating a straight vertical line from hip to the ball of the foot, while the opposite leg is lifted with the knee bent at approximately 90 degrees and held slightly out to the side for balance. The standing leg's knee remains fully extended and locked, the torso stays erect without leaning, and the calf muscle of the supporting leg appears fully contracted and defined. The hand lightly touches the wall or railing for stability as the body faces forward.

name: Single Leg Deadlift
pose_description: Standing on one leg with a slight bend in the standing knee. The torso hinges forward at the hips while the non-standing leg extends straight behind, creating a T shape with the body. The arms hang down or hold a weight, the back remains flat, and the hips stay squared to the floor. The movement is a controlled hip hinge with the hamstrings and glutes of the standing leg working eccentrically.
end_pose_description: The torso is nearly parallel to the ground in a deep hip hinge, with the standing leg's knee slightly bent and the non-standing leg extended straight back at hip height, forming a perfect horizontal line from the back leg through the torso. The back remains flat and rigid, the arms hang vertically downward (or hold a weight at the hips), and the standing leg's hamstrings and glutes appear fully engaged and tensioned. The person faces downward with their gaze following the neutral spine alignment.

name: Single-Leg Deadlift with Dumbbell
pose_description: Stand upright on your left leg holding a dumbbell in your right hand at your side with a slight knee bend. Keep your core engaged and shoulders back.
end_pose_description: The torso is hinged forward at the hips, nearly parallel to the floor, with the back straight and the left glute and hamstring visibly engaged. The right leg is extended straight backward, forming a line from the head to the right heel, while the right arm hangs straight down, the dumbbell close to the floor. The erector spinae muscles of the back are visibly engaged, and the hamstring of the standing left leg is under stretch.

name: Single-Leg Deadlifts with Dumbbells
pose_description: Stand on one leg holding a dumbbell in the opposite hand, maintaining a slight bend in your standing knee. Keep your chest up and engage your core for stability.
end_pose_description: Hinge at the hip while extending your free leg behind you for balance, lowering the dumbbell toward the ground. Return to standing by driving through your heel and squeezing your glute.

name: Single-Leg Deadlifts with Dumbbell
pose_description: Stand on one leg holding a dumbbell in the opposite hand, with a slight knee bend in the standing leg. Keep your chest upright and core engaged.
end_pose_description: Hinge forward at the hip while extending the non-standing leg behind you for balance, lowering the dumbbell toward the ground. Return to standing by driving through the heel of the support leg.

name: Single-Leg Deadlifts with Dumbbells
pose_description: Stand on one leg while holding dumbbells at your sides, with a slight bend in your standing knee. Your non-working leg is relaxed and your gaze is fixed forward to maintain balance.
end_pose_description: Your torso is hinged forward at the hip, nearly parallel to the floor, with the dumbbells hanging straight down towards the ground, and your standing knee maintains its slight bend. Your non-working leg is extended straight back and level with your torso, with the hamstrings of the standing leg visibly stretched and the glutes and erector spinae engaged; your gaze is fixed on the floor.

name: Single-Leg Dumbbell Deadlift
pose_description: Stand on one leg with a slight knee bend, holding a dumbbell in the opposite hand at your side. Your standing leg is stable and your core is engaged.
end_pose_description: Stand upright, balanced on one leg with a slight knee bend, the dumbbell held in the opposite hand at your side. Your glutes and hamstrings are visibly engaged, your back is straight, and your core is braced.

name: Single-Leg Glute Bridge
pose_description: Lying supine with hips still on the floor (NOT yet bridged). ONLY the left foot is flat on the floor with the left knee bent at about 90 degrees. The RIGHT leg is clearly lifted into the air: right foot is suspended 4-6 inches above the floor with the right knee bent at roughly 90 degrees. CRITICAL: only ONE foot is on the floor — both feet planted is wrong, this is NOT a regular two-leg glute bridge.
end_pose_description: Hips are bridged high off the floor, supported by the LEFT foot ONLY. Torso, hips, and left thigh form a straight diagonal line from shoulders to left knee. The RIGHT leg remains suspended in the air with the knee bent at roughly 90 degrees — the right foot is clearly NOT touching the floor. CRITICAL: only ONE foot is on the floor — both feet planted is wrong, this is NOT a regular two-leg glute bridge.

name: Single-Leg Glute Bridges with Dumbbell
pose_description: Lie on your back with one knee bent and foot flat on the ground, the other leg extended straight up. Hold a dumbbell across your hips with both hands.
end_pose_description: Drive through your planted foot to lift your hips toward the ceiling, creating a straight line from knee to shoulders. Squeeze your glutes at the top before lowering back down.

name: Single-Leg Romanian Deadlift with Band
pose_description: Stand on one leg while holding a resistance band anchored under the standing foot. Maintain an upright posture with a slight knee bend in the standing leg.
end_pose_description: Hinge at the hip and extend the non-standing leg behind you for balance while leaning your torso forward. Feel the stretch and engagement in the hamstring of the standing leg as you return to upright.

name: Single Leg Romanian Deadlift
pose_description: Stand on one leg holding a dumbbell in the opposite hand with a slight knee bend. Your standing leg is engaged and your core is tight.
end_pose_description: Your torso is hinged forward from the hips, almost parallel to the floor, with a straight back and a neutral head. The dumbbell hangs straight down close to the shin of your standing leg, which maintains its slight knee bend, while your non-standing leg is extended straight back, level with your torso. The hamstring and glute of the standing leg are fully stretched and engaged, and your core is tightly braced to maintain this aligned position.

name: Single Leg Squats
pose_description: Stand upright on one leg with the other leg lifted slightly in front of you, arms extended forward for balance. Keep your chest upright and core engaged.
end_pose_description: Lower your body by bending the standing leg's knee to approximately 45-60 degrees, keeping your torso upright and weight in your heel. The lifted leg remains extended or slightly bent for counterbalance.

name: Single Leg Stance
pose_description: Stand with feet hip-width apart, arms at sides or ready to use nearby support. Engage your core and maintain upright posture.
end_pose_description: Your weight is fully supported by one leg, with the opposing foot suspended just off the floor. The standing leg's glutes, quadriceps, and calf muscles are visibly taut, maintaining a stable and upright torso. Arms are positioned slightly away from the body, offering counter-balance.

name: Single Leg Stance - Dynamic
pose_description: Stand on one leg with the other knee lifted to hip height, with hands on your hips or extended to the sides for balance. Keep your focus on a fixed point ahead.
end_pose_description: Hold the single-leg stance for 20-30 seconds while maintaining upright posture and a fixed gaze. Your standing leg should be slightly bent at the knee for stability.

name: Single Leg Stance with Upper Body Support
pose_description: Stand facing a sturdy gym railing or wall with fingertips lightly touching for support. Feet are hip-width apart with weight evenly distributed.
end_pose_description: Lift one foot slightly off the ground while maintaining light contact with the support. Keep your core engaged and gaze fixed on a stable point ahead.

name: Single Leg Stand
pose_description: Stand upright with feet hip-width apart and arms at your sides or extended for balance. Look straight ahead with a neutral spine.
end_pose_description: One foot is lifted clear of the floor, with the knee slightly bent and the foot suspended freely. The entire body weight rests on the opposite standing leg, with the ankle stabilizers and calf muscles (gastrocnemius, soleus) visibly taut to maintain balance, and the gluteus medius engaged to keep the hips level. The torso remains upright with a neutral spine, and the arms are extended to the sides for balance while the gaze holds straight ahead.

name: Standing Balance on One Leg
pose_description: Stand upright with your hand on a wall or counter for light support. Your weight is evenly distributed on both feet.
end_pose_description: Your body is upright, with your hand resting lightly on the wall or counter. All your weight rests on one foot, with the other foot lifted a few inches from the floor and its knee gently bent. The muscles of the standing leg and your core are visibly engaged to maintain balance.

name: Standing Balance on One Leg
pose_description: Stand upright with your hand on a wall or rail for light support if needed. Both feet are on the ground, shoulder-width apart.
end_pose_description: The body is upright, balanced on one straight leg with the foot of the other leg lifted several inches off the ground, knee slightly bent. The gluteus medius, quadriceps, and calf of the standing leg are visibly engaged, and hands maintain light contact with the wall or rail if needed for stability.

name: Standing Single-Leg Balance
pose_description: Stand upright with feet hip-width apart, hands resting on a wall or sturdy chair. Keep your core engaged and eyes focused on a fixed point.
end_pose_description: Lift one foot off the ground, balancing on the other leg while maintaining an upright posture. Hold the position for 10-30 seconds, using the chair for light support as needed.

name: Standing Single Leg Balance with Band
pose_description: Stand upright facing a wall or support surface with hands lightly on the support. Anchor a resistance band at waist height for added stability if needed.
end_pose_description: Shift weight to one leg and lift the opposite foot slightly off the ground, maintaining balance. Hold briefly, then lower and switch sides.

name: Standing Single-Leg Balance with Hip Stability
pose_description: Standing on one leg with the standing knee slightly bent, focusing on keeping the pelvis level without dropping on the unsupported side. The non-standing leg is lifted with the knee bent to approximately 90 degrees of hip flexion. Arms are at sides or on hips, the torso is tall, and the gluteus medius of the standing leg is actively engaged to maintain pelvic stability.
end_pose_description: The person stands tall on one leg with a slightly bent knee, maintaining a perfectly level pelvis without any lateral drop, while the opposite leg remains lifted with the knee bent at approximately 90 degrees of hip flexion and positioned in front of the body. The torso is upright and centered over the standing leg's foot, with visible tension through the glutes and hip stabilizers of the standing side, while the arms are either relaxed at the sides or resting on the hips, and the gaze is fixed forward.

name: Standing Single-Leg Calf Raises
pose_description: Stand upright on one leg with your hands lightly touching a wall or rail for balance. Keep your core engaged and your standing leg slightly bent.
end_pose_description: Rise up onto the ball of your foot, lifting your heel off the ground as high as possible. Lower back down with control and repeat on the same leg before switching sides.

name: Standing Single-Leg Stance
pose_description: Stand upright with feet hip-width apart near a wall or sturdy chair for safety support. Keep your arms ready to grasp support if needed.
end_pose_description: Shift your weight onto one leg and lift the opposite foot slightly off the ground, maintaining an upright posture. Keep your eyes focused on a fixed point ahead.

name: Standing Single-Leg Stance with Band Support
pose_description: Stand facing a wall or sturdy surface with a resistance band looped around a post at waist height for light support. Feet are together.
end_pose_description: Lift one leg slightly off the ground and balance on the standing leg while maintaining light contact with the band. Hold for 20-30 seconds, then switch legs.

name: Standing Single Leg Stand
pose_description: Stand next to a wall or counter with your hand resting lightly on it for support. Position your feet hip-width apart with your weight evenly distributed.
end_pose_description: Shift your weight onto one leg while lifting the other foot slightly off the ground. Maintain an upright posture and hold this position for 10-30 seconds.

name: Suitcase Carry
pose_description: Stand upright holding a dumbbell in one hand at your side with a neutral spine. Your shoulders are level and your core is engaged.
end_pose_description: Stand upright with a neutral spine, holding the dumbbell in one hand at your side. Your shoulders are level, actively resisting the lateral pull of the weight. The obliques on the side opposite the dumbbell are strongly contracted, and the gluteus medius on the unweighted side is actively engaged, maintaining a stable and level pelvis.

name: Suitcase Carry with Dumbbell
pose_description: Stand upright holding a dumbbell in one hand at your side with your arm extended, shoulders level and squared. Engage your core to prevent side bending.
end_pose_description: The body stands upright, arm extended at the side, holding the dumbbell, with shoulders level and squared and hips horizontally aligned. The obliques and quadratus lumborum on the side opposite the dumbbell are visibly contracted, and the erector spinae muscles along the back are engaged, maintaining a neutral spine. The upper trapezius and deltoids on the loaded side also show engagement, stabilizing the shoulder.
